bull.b: The long-dated Rockdale lease could shift Riot toward recurring infrastructure revenue with substantially higher visibility than standalone Bitcoin mining. Its contracted scale and projected NOI margins create a durable growth platform, provided the company executes the phased buildout and financing plan.

Riot’s large deployed hash rate and low reported power cost support competitiveness in a network where electricity and operating efficiency are core inputs. These capabilities can improve resilience and preserve mining economics relative to less efficient operators over the next several quarters.

The engineering segment adds an operating capability beyond Bitcoin production and is increasingly tied to data-center demand. Rising revenue, improved margins, and a mostly data-center backlog can support execution, reduce reliance on external contractors, and reinforce Riot’s infrastructure expansion.

bear.b: Riot’s strong revenue growth has not translated into sustainable profits, with negative gross margin and substantial net losses indicating a weak current cost structure. Persistent losses reduce internal funding capacity and make future earnings highly sensitive to operating conditions and asset values.

Ongoing operating and free-cash-flow deficits mean Riot is consuming capital while pursuing a capital-intensive expansion. This can increase reliance on financing, asset sales, or additional equity and may constrain strategic flexibility if project spending rises faster than cash generation.

bear.t: High exposure to Bitcoin mining conditions
bear.b: Bitcoin mining remains a major earnings driver, leaving Riot exposed to cryptocurrency prices, network competition, and power economics. These factors can change faster than infrastructure contracts, creating meaningful earnings volatility and complicating the transition toward steadier data-center revenue.
